speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light over the last two days? Also, have you had any recent travel, tick bites, or contact with sick individuals?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I am concerned about a potential neuroleptic malignant syndrome or severe extrapyramidal side effect. Can you tell me if you have experienced any muscle rigidity, tremors, or excessive sweating, and have you recently started or increased your dose of haloperidol?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, altered mentation, profuse sweating, and generalized rigidity in the context of haloperidol use is classic for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will confirm this by checking for elevated muscle enzymes and white blood cell count. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase; Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Complete Blood Count - White Blood Cell Count: 14,700/mm3 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: The markedly elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis confirm the diagnosis of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
